subject.title: MEDIA: tokens inside markdown code fences are silently ignored

question: Should fenced legacy `MEDIA:` directives remain non-extracting with a warning, be extracted as attachments, or stay docs-only/by-design?
rationale: Current code intentionally treats fenced lines as examples, but the report shows a real silent media-delivery failure; extraction versus diagnostics changes the product contract and false-positive risk.

options.title: Warn Only At Delivery Boundary
options.body: Keep fenced tokens as visible text, emit one diagnostic warning in the actual outbound delivery path, and resolve the open warn-only PR.

options.title: Extract From Fences
options.body: Treat standalone fenced `MEDIA:` lines as attachments, accepting the risk that code examples can become deliverable media unless a stricter policy is designed.

options.title: Docs Only
options.body: Keep runtime behavior unchanged and rely on documentation that legacy `MEDIA:` lines must be standalone plain text.

recommendation.title: Warn Only At Delivery Boundary
recommendation.body: Keep fenced tokens as visible text, emit one diagnostic warning in the actual outbound delivery path, and resolve the open warn-only PR.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has recent media/reply-path history and the live review asking for a delivery-boundary warning contract on the linked PR.
